history.content:
Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

history.content:
Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

# minimal psycopg2 stub so contrib.postgres.forms can import
pg = types.ModuleType('psycopg2')

from django.contrib.postgres.forms import SplitArrayField

class F(forms.Form):
    flags = SplitArrayField(forms.BooleanField(required=False), size=4)
    flags2 = SplitArrayField(forms.BooleanField(required=False), size=3)

f = F(initial={'flags': [True, False, True, False], 'flags2': [False, False, False]})

assert checked == [True, False, True, False, False, False, False], checked

# attrs mutation check on CheckboxInput directly
w = forms.CheckboxInput()
attrs = {'class': 'x'}
ctx = w.get_context('n', True, attrs)
assert attrs == {'class': 'x'}, attrs
assert ctx['widget']['attrs']['checked'] is True
assert w.get_context('n', False, {'checked': False})['widget']['attrs'].get('checked') is False
# attrs=None path
assert w.get_context('n', True, None)['widget']['attrs']['checked'] is True
print('OK: no attrs mutation, correct checked states')
EOF

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

# 1. Root cause: CheckboxInput must not mutate the caller's attrs dict.
w = CheckboxInput()
attrs = {'class': 'x'}

assert w.get_context('n', True, None)['widget']['attrs']['checked'] is True
assert 'checked' not in w.get_context('n', False, None)['widget']['attrs']

# 2. Reuse of the SAME dict across repeated calls (the SplitArrayWidget pattern).
shared = {'class': 'y'}
first = w.get_context('a', True, shared)['widget']['attrs']
second = w.get_context('b', False, shared)['widget']['attrs']
third = w.get_context('c', True, shared)['widget']['attrs']

    flags2 = SplitArrayField(forms.BooleanField(required=False), size=3)

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

from django.conf import settings
settings.configure(
    DEBUG=True, USE_TZ=True, INSTALLED_APPS=['django.contrib.contenttypes', 'django.contrib.auth'],

from django import forms
from django.forms.widgets import CheckboxInput

# 1. Root cause: CheckboxInput must not mutate the caller's attrs dict.
w = CheckboxInput()
attrs = {'class': 'x'}
ctx = w.get_context('n', True, attrs)
assert attrs == {'class': 'x'}, 'attrs mutated: %r' % attrs
assert ctx['widget']['attrs']['checked'] is True
assert ctx['widget']['attrs']['class'] == 'x'
# False value must not add 'checked'
assert 'checked' not in w.get_context('n', False, {'class': 'x'})['widget']['attrs']
assert w.get_context('n', True, None)['widget']['attrs']['checked'] is True
assert 'checked' not in w.get_context('n', False, None)['widget']['attrs']

# 2. Reuse of the SAME dict across repeated calls (the SplitArrayWidget pattern).
shared = {'class': 'y'}
first = w.get_context('a', True, shared)['widget']['attrs']
second = w.get_context('b', False, shared)['widget']['attrs']
third = w.get_context('c', True, shared)['widget']['attrs']
assert first['checked'] is True and 'checked' not in second and third['checked'] is True, (first, second, third)
assert shared == {'class': 'y'}, shared
print('CheckboxInput OK')

# 3. SplitArrayWidget/Field rendering, using a bool base field.
import sys, types
pg = types.ModuleType('psycopg2'); extras = types.ModuleType('psycopg2.extras')
class _R:
    def __init__(self, *a, **k): pass
extras.DateRange = extras.DateTimeTZRange = extras.NumericRange = _R
pg.extras = extras
sys.modules.setdefault('psycopg2', pg); sys.modules.setdefault('psycopg2.extras', extras)
from django.contrib.postgres.forms import SplitArrayField, SplitArrayWidget

class F(forms.Form):
    flags = SplitArrayField(forms.BooleanField(required=False), size=4)
    flags2 = SplitArrayField(forms.BooleanField(required=False), size=3)

f = F(initial={'flags': [True, False, True, False], 'flags2': [False, False, False]})
html = f.as_p()
checked = ['checked' in seg for seg in re.findall(r'<input[^>]*>', html)]
print('checked pattern:', checked)
assert checked == [True, False, True, False, False, False, False], checked

# Leading-False case must stay unchecked even after a later True.
f2 = F(initial={'flags': [False, False, False, True]})
checked2 = ['checked' in seg for seg in re.findall(r'<input[^>]*>', f2.as_p())]
print('leading-false pattern:', checked2)
assert checked2 == [False, False, False, True, False, False, False], checked2

# Unbound form with no initial data renders all unchecked, and ids are per-index.
f3 = F()
html3 = f3.as_p()
assert html3.count('checked') == 0, html3
ids = re.findall(r'id="(id_flags[^"]*)"', html3)
print('ids:', ids)
assert ids == ['id_flags_0', 'id_flags_1', 'id_flags_2', 'id_flags_3'], ids

# Widget-level context check: subwidgets independent, caller attrs untouched.
widget = SplitArrayWidget(forms.CheckboxInput(), size=3)
outer = {'class': 'z'}
c = widget.get_context('w', [True, False, True], outer)
subs = [s['attrs'] for s in c['widget']['subwidgets']]
print('subwidget attrs:', subs)
assert [bool(s.get('checked')) for s in subs] == [True, False, True]
assert outer == {'class': 'z'}, outer
print('ALL OK')

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

shared = {'class': 'y'}
